story.vex: Improvised walls fall to a patient enemy. Show me your rulebook, Captain — oh, you don't have one. (Commander Vex, Planet Doom)
story.victory: DOOM ATTACK REPELLED before it started: every gap is mapped and closed. Astro: "Guesses don't scale. A framework does. Now we can prove it, not just hope it."

files.C:\\Citadel\\README.txt:
ORDERS FROM ASTRO
=================
Astro wants proof our defenses follow a real rulebook, not guesses. Read nist-mapping.txt, then map each Citadel defense to its NIST CSF function: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond or Recover.
files.C:\\Citadel\\nist-mapping.txt:
NIST Cybersecurity Framework — the five functions
---------------------------------------------------
Identify  — know your assets and risks (the inventory from Lesson 1.1)
Protect   — lock things down before an attack (passwords, icacls, the AUP)
Detect    — notice an attack while it's happening (Volt's sensors, the logs)
Respond   — act once you've detected something (disabling accounts, killing processes)
Recover   — get back to normal after (restoring from backup)

Citadel defenses to map:
asset-inventory   -> the crew's list of what to protect
relay-password    -> the strong password policy on the relay console
volt-sensors      -> the alarm that first caught the 02:47 intrusion
incident-response -> disabling svc_update and closing its port
backup-restore     -> currently MISSING — we have no Detect step for it yet

steps.title: Map five defenses to five functions
steps.body: Astro: "Guesses don't scale. A framework does." Read `nist-mapping.txt`, then classify each defense to its function: `classify asset-inventory identify`, `classify relay-password protect`, and so on. The note flags `backup-restore` as missing a Detect step — fix that one by giving it the function it's actually missing, `detect`.
